correctness.rationale: The exact circulant eigenvalue equals a strictly positive periodized Gaussian theta series minus an omitted Gaussian tail. Poisson summation supplies a uniform lower exponent -pi^2 n/(4c); the tail is uniformly O(exp(-cn/4)). For c>pi the positive periodization dominates all frequencies. For c<pi, even- and odd-cycle high-frequency choices have explicitly positive omitted-tail leading terms (tanh(c/2) for even lengths, and pi*delta/n*exp(-c/2)*(1-exp(-c))/(1+exp(-c))^2 for odd lengths), with the Poisson term exponentially smaller. Dominated convergence is justified by geometric Gaussian majorants and the sine Lipschitz bound; the unit-edge normalization and delta in {1,3} have been checked. Positivity of the Schur map iff the mask is PSD follows from the Schur product theorem and its action on the all-ones positive matrix. A 118-check high-precision direct DFT/periodization test passed as supplementary evidence, not as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The c=pi boundary resolves a natural dimension-varying sampling question for geodesic Gaussian kernels. It separates completely positive Schur transformations from maps failing even positivity, in a setting where continuous-circle Gaussian kernels fail positive definiteness at every fixed physical parameter. The exact sharp rate and parity-resolved negative witnesses are substantive finite-to-continuum spectral information, related to an explicitly stated quantitative question in arXiv:2303.06558. This is not merely a finite table or sign computation; it holds for every sufficiently large cycle with fixed c off the boundary.
